parsed_response.reasoning: The `minimumTokenResponseSchema` in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` which evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' (duplicate keys, last one wins), so the schema effectively only requires `access_token` plus a meaningless '[object Object]' optional field. In sharing mode this replaces the real app schema (e.g. `zoomRefreshedTokenSchema`, `refreshTokenResponseSchema`), and z.object strips unknown keys, so fields like `expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, `scope`, `token_type` are silently dropped (the code then fabricates `refresh_token: "refresh_token"`). This breaks token refresh for Zoom, Google, O365, Salesforce in credential-sharing mode. The finding's exact mechanism (index signatures 'rejecting' string fields) is slightly off — the real defect is stripping/corrupting the parsed data — but the substantive claim that the new schema breaks refresh in sharing mode is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` tries to express “any numeric field” / “allow other properties” using computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, but in a JS object literal that becomes a single literal property name (e.g. "ZodString"/"[object Object]") rather than an index signature/catchall. Zod will then require that exact property to exist (and be a number), so `safeParse(response)` in sharing mode will likely fail for real OAuth token responses and throw "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". This can break refresh flows when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set.
